doc.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995

chapter: Naming the music, family and Bix
title: Meeting the surviving Goldkette band members
summary: Through the Bix concerts he met Venuti, Ryker, Morehouse and Spiegle Willcox, and values contact with living history.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Bix? Well one of the interesting things about that series of concerts was that they had everybody that was still alive from the Goldkette band involved in that concert at one time or another, so while I never met Bix, I hung out with Joe Venuti, I hung out with Doc Ryker who was the lead alto saxophone, Chauncey Morehouse the drummer was still alive, Spiegle Willcox, who may be here tomorrow, is still alive living in Cincinnatus, New York. You ought to go over and see him.
My goodness, thanks for that information.

Oh, he’s a pistol, too. He’s just absolutely as bright as a tack. He was in the Goldkette band with all those guys. But everybody that had anything to do with the Goldkette band was at one point or other part of that series of concerts. And I’ve always — I have a sense of history that gives me a great deal of pleasure when I get to meet and interact with people that have experienced something.
I know what you mean. This has been like that for us.
